prior_decision.quote: To complement the survey results, a bibliometric approach was used to identify replications in the TIS literature by carrying out a conceptual replication of Makel, Plucker, and Hegarty’s (2012) study on replication in psychology research. While the original study was conducted by analyzing only 100 journals with the highest 5-year impact factor in the field of psychology, in the present study, the bibliometric analysis was carried out using BITRA (Franco Aixelá 2001–2019).
prior_decision.location: Section 3.2 Study 2: Bibliometric analysis of replications in BITRA, lines 836-843 (with comparisons in Section 5.2, lines 2368-2425)
prior_decision.reason: Omitted target in the shipped dataset. Study 2 explicitly conducts a conceptual replication of Makel, Plucker, and Hegarty (2012) using the BITRA database and directly compares its bibliometric findings against Makel et al. (2012) in Section 5.2. Those comparisons are mixed: the author notes that the overall published replication rate is higher in psychology (1.07% vs. 0.06% in BITRA) and that self-replications make up 52.9% of replications in Makel et al. (2012) versus 30.4% in BITRA (where replications of others' studies predominate at 65.2%), while the low proportion of exact replications is described as not very different from Makel et al. (8.7% in BITRA vs. 14% in psychology).

luna_triage.reason: Study 2 explicitly conducts a conceptual replication of Makel et al. (2012), and the discussion compares replication prevalence, self-replication proportions, and exact-replication proportions with that work. The supplied row 123 is Yeung (2017), a different study, and does not represent Makel et al.
